# What stubtest cannot check, and why.
#
# GENERATED from platform_api/facade.pyi by generator/generate.py.  Do not edit:
# regenerate.  Being generated is the point -- an allowlist maintained by hand
# grows an entry every time someone wants a failure to go away, and this one
# can only ever contain the aliases the stub declares.
#
# Nothing else belongs here.  A real disagreement between the stub and the
# generated code is the one thing the gate exists to catch.
#
# The first group is `Literal[...]` type aliases.  They are emitted into
# facade.py as well as declared in the stub, so a consumer can reach the
# permitted values through typing.get_args(); but a runtime `Literal` object is
# not a Union as far as stubtest is concerned, and it reports the alias as
# mismatched however it is spelled.  typeshed allowlists its own for the same
# reason.

platform_api.facade.ChangeEventKind

# a projected snapshot as returning its rows; the generator gives the method a
# `cols` parameter and emits the `<Row>Cols` bit constants beside it.  Neither
# is spelled in the stub because both are derived from that one declaration,
# and writing them there as well would be a second copy to drift.
